description: The Mexican research team publishes medical-support vehicle location and allocation scenarios anchored to the 2017 Mexico City earthquake. The Zenodo package combines administrative, population, building-impact and street-network layers with synthetic casualty demand points. Eight Python notebooks describe preprocessing and scenario preparation. Public data and derived layers are free under CC BY-NC 4.0; the scripts have a separate GPL 3.0 notice. The scenarios support emergency vehicle placement, coverage and travel-time optimisation in disaster simulations. TomTom traffic data are not redistributed and require a separate API key. Synthetic victim locations and source-date differences limit direct use as historical observations. Notebook execution and geospatial consistency were not tested. No directly related catalogue dataset was identified. This limits direct comparison with actual ambulance deployments. Use as a historical ambulance deployment record is limited.
